Tool names here are Academic Harness's own. In Claude Code, `subagent` is `Agent`, `skill` is `Skill`, and `mcp__papermemory__*` is `mcp__plugin_academic-harness_papermemory__*`. If a tool named below is not in your tool list, say so.

## Reproducible analysis

For any analysis whose numbers may be reported, run it through `analysis_run`, not ad-hoc shell: `plan` freezes question, inputs, outputs, methods, alpha, exclusions, stopping rules, and seed before execution (changing a frozen plan needs `new_version: true` plus a reason); `run` executes an argv command with an environment allowlist, hashed inputs/outputs, a hard timeout, and redacted logs, and appends a lab-notebook entry; `expect` declares the reported numbers (value, output path, json/csv/tsv/kv/regex parsing, tolerance, and a reported|reproduced reference) and `verify_scores` re-hashes and compares a later run's hashed outputs, writing `repro_check.json` with true/false/not_checked — changed output bytes, a failed, timed-out, different-plan, changed-entrypoint, or changed-interpreter run is not_checked, never a silent mismatch. `diff` compares runs or a run against the current plan; the manifest — not a copied notebook output — is the evidence. Use `experiment_log` for sweeps and staged comparisons: declare the benchmark (datasets, splits, baseline arm, task rules) and protocol at start; log `role` baseline|variant, `baseline_ref` reproduced|reported, `stage` subset|slice|full, and a sampling rule; the baseline captures a protocol digest and every variant must match its baseline reference, with a changed eval script or metric parameters reported as `spec_drift`; `best` is by a named metric and direction or the multi-metric Pareto front with `dominance`, and `verdict` records good|engineer|bad, force-bad when the engineering budget is exhausted (a rerun is a new run); `compliance` checks a run against the plan's frozen task rules (machine checks or caller evidence) and a violating run is excluded from best and from repro_package/deposit, never refined. `dataset_get` to download DOI-registered datasets with checksums and licenses into `data/<slug>/` (`dataset_search` stays search-only); `data_profile` to profile a local file before analysis — its leakage and split-overlap flags are risks for review, and its `not_checked` list means never "safe". Finish a paper or project with `repro_package`: a frozen inventory built into a reader-facing package (manifest, environment, Dockerfile, README, CITATION.cff, RO-Crate, checksums); a compliance-violating run is omitted and listed under `excluded_runs`, and its Zenodo deposit is preview-gated, draft-only, and never publishes for you. Load the `reproducible-analysis` and `experiment-tracking` skills.

For experiment rankings, log a user-declared comparison_identity for every staged run and name baseline_run_id explicitly for every staged variant, matching its baseline's stage and sampling. Inspect scope IDs with experiment_log compare; pass the selected scope_id to best, dominance, compare, or export. For repeated seeds, use experiment_log replicates with an explicit scope, candidate labels, replicate unit, and expected seeds or explicitly unknown coverage. Report duplicate/missing/failed runs and baseline-linked same-seed pairs; its means and sample SDs are descriptive, not significance tests or proof of independence. To trace ancestry and links, use experiment_log branches (text by default, json, or escaped mermaid); its status is evidence-only — failed requires a resolved linked execution failure or timeout, pruned requires a recorded bad verdict, and missing metrics never mean failed — and only format=mermaid with write=true writes exports/branches.mmd. Never rank historical runs without identity, protocol drift, incompatible scopes, or unresolved compliance evidence. A matching scope is a declaration, not scientific verification.

For a focused research workflow, load `limitation-mining` for quoted flaws and bounded sufficiency, `novelty-triage` for a grounded prior-art reading, `subset-first-eval` for a frozen subset-to-full benchmark, `method-code-alignment` for reviewed source bindings, and `integrity-audit` for the four-column advisory reading. A general request to explore is not approval to run, spend, upload, review, edit, or deposit. Seek permission before running analyses or new review rounds. Never mix reported and reproduced baselines, invent a quote, turn `not_checked` into a pass, or silently promote a champion.
